cards.title: BAIR Papers at CoRL 2026: Humanoid Control, Dexterous Manipulation, and Agentic Robotics
cards.why_it_matters: CoRL is a top robotics-learning venue and this overview flags which BAIR papers on VLA models, RL-for-robots, and humanoid control are worth reading in the coming weeks.
cards.summary: Berkeley AI Research presents 20+ papers at CoRL 2026 (Austin, Nov 9–12) spanning generalist robot policies, multi-scale embodied memory for VLA models, dexterous manipulation with egocentric data (EgoScale), humanoid whole-body control via a differentiable world model (SuperMimic), flow-based policy gradients, and agentic self-improvement. An Early Career Keynote is delivered by Prof. Negar Mehr.

cards.title: Chiral Waveguide Atom-Photon Scattering Linked to QEC Threshold and Algorithmic Design
cards.why_it_matters: Bridges microscopic photonic hardware models to quantum error correction thresholds, offering a path for co-designing photonic qubit systems with error-corrected algorithms.
cards.summary: A first-principles framework derives an effective polarization quantum channel for single photons scattering off two-level atoms in a chiral waveguide. Applied as the noise model for a rotated planar code, threshold behavior emerges as a function of atom number N, coupling Γ, and photon bandwidth σ, scaling as NΓ/σ. The resulting noise is strongly X-biased; a Hadamard-basis QPE implementation exploits this bias to improve algorithmic performance.

cards.title: Patterned TiN Stressor Films Proposed to Deterministically Boost Valley Splitting in Si/SiGe Spin Qubits
cards.why_it_matters: Random valley splitting is a key scalability obstacle for silicon spin qubits; a fabrication-compatible deterministic solution is directly relevant to near-term quantum hardware scaling.
cards.summary: Compressively stressed TiN thin films patterned on Si/SiGe quantum dot devices are proposed to generate deterministic shear strain in the quantum well. Finite-element simulations show shear strains exceeding 0.1% at the well, sufficient for valley splittings of hundreds of μeV in strain-assisted Wiggle Wells. The strain extends across multiple dots and is maintained in realistic gate geometries, making it compatible with quantum dot arrays.

cards.title: GARI++: Two-Stage General-Purpose QEC Decoder Achieves Near-MWPM Accuracy with FPGA Latencies from 201 ns
cards.why_it_matters: Real-time decoding latency and cross-code generality are critical for practical QEC; GARI++'s FPGA-CPU hybrid pipeline with sub-microsecond first-stage latencies is a concrete engineering advance.
cards.summary: GARI++ pipelines a normalized min-sum first-stage decoder (GARI) with a configurable second-stage decoder for cases that don't converge. At physical error rate 0.001 under circuit-level depolarizing noise, the FPGA GARI stage achieves latencies of 201 ns to 11.8 μs for surface code distances 7–25. Residual decoding on a single Apple M2 core stays below one microsecond up to distance 51 using Union-Find, with accuracy on par with correlated MWPM.

cards.title: Dephasing Algebraically Suppresses Bragg Peaks in Spectral Form Factors of Open Quantum Systems
cards.why_it_matters: Establishes spectral form factors as a probe of spectral order in open systems, relevant for quantum error correction and quantum simulation where environmental dephasing is unavoidable.
cards.summary: This work analyzes how energy dephasing in open quantum systems erodes long-range spectral order visible as Bragg peaks in the spectral form factor. Peaks fade algebraically with revival order p and dephasing strength γ as K_Bragg(p) ∝ (γp)^{-1/2} within an intermediate regime, yet persist until nearest-neighbor coherences decay. Temporal correlations in spectral fluctuations are identified as a control handle.

cards.title: Closed-Form Hidden Symmetry Operators Derived for Asymmetric Quantum Rabi Model and Variants
cards.why_it_matters: Provides exact analytic symmetry operators for a foundational light-matter coupling model used in superconducting and photonic qubit architectures, enabling cleaner theoretical analysis of level crossings.
cards.summary: The asymmetric quantum Rabi model exhibits level crossings at integer-multiple biases due to a hidden symmetry operator J, previously lacking a general formula. This work derives J in closed form for every integer bias N as the parity operator of the symmetric model times a continuant of N first-order operators. The same construction extends to asymmetric two-photon and two-mode variants via su(1,1) generators.

cards.title: NVIDIA & Elith Release Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan: 9M Synthetic Japanese Financial Personas
cards.why_it_matters: Synthetic data generation pipelines using PGMs and LLMs for domain-specific finance are directly relevant to anyone building or evaluating financial AI agents without access to real customer data.
cards.summary: Elith and NVIDIA have released a 9M-persona (~1.5B token) synthetic dataset grounding Japan's official demographic and labor statistics with household finance and financial literacy data. Built via NeMo SDG-PGMs (probabilistic graphical models) and NeMo Data Designer using Gemma-4-31B-it for Japanese text generation, it covers 50 fields per record and 1600+ occupations. Licensed CC BY 4.0 for commercial use.

cards.title: HOPE: Second-Order MoE Expert Pruning Beats First-Order Methods by Up to +6.1% on Coding Tasks
cards.why_it_matters: MoE memory footprint is a major practical bottleneck, and HOPE's pairwise-interaction-aware pruning is a training-free, quantization-compatible technique directly applicable to models like Qwen or Mixtral.
cards.summary: HOPE (Higher-Order Pruning of Experts) replaces scalar per-expert importance scores with a second-order method that accounts for pairwise co-activation patterns among experts. At 50% pruning rate, HOPE achieves the best average rank across benchmarks and gains up to +6.1% over the next-best pruning method on agentic coding tasks. It requires no retraining and composes with quantization.
